40 Which statement about the alpha-particle scattering experiment provides evidence for the
existence of the nucleus?
A
A tiny proportion of the alpha-particles are deflected through large angles.
B
Slower alpha-particles are deflected through larger angles.
C
The kinetic energies of the deflected alpha-particles are unchanged.
D
The number of alpha-particles deflected depends on the thickness of the foil.

hints: Notice the question asks for evidence for the existence of the nucleus, and that most alpha-particles pass through the gold foil almost undeflected.
Connect a large-angle deflection of a positive $+2e$ alpha-particle to the need for a very strong electrostatic repulsion from a concentrated positive charge.
Compare a tiny proportion suffering large deflection with the majority passing straight through to infer the deflecting centre must be very small compared with the atom.
walkthrough: Recall the experiment: alpha-particles are fired at thin gold foil and most pass straight through, while very few are scattered.
State the governing physics: an alpha-particle is positively charged, so deflection is caused by electrostatic repulsion from positive charge in the atom.
A large-angle deflection, including backscattering through more than $90^{\circ}$, needs a very large force acting over a short distance.
Such a force can only come from all the positive charge being concentrated in a tiny volume, so a direct hit produces huge repulsion while distant passes give almost no deflection.
The observation that only a tiny proportion are affected shows that this concentrated centre occupies only a very small fraction of the atomic volume.
That small, dense, positively charged centre is the nucleus. This is option A.

A.explanation: Only a tiny, dense region of concentrated positive charge can exert the very large electrostatic repulsion needed to turn an alpha-particle through a large angle on a rare head-on approach.

B.explanation: Larger deflection for slower alpha-particles shows the Coulomb repulsion acts for longer, but it does not by itself prove charge is concentrated in a nucleus.

C.explanation: Unchanged kinetic energy shows the scattering is elastic with a massive target, but it does not prove the positive charge occupies a tiny nucleus.

D.explanation: More scattering with thicker foil shows alpha-particles meet more gold atoms, but it does not prove each atom has a small central nucleus.
